entries: Literally, “night of the long knives”. The term had been in use since at least 1932 for a murderous reckoning that the Nazis were expected to conduct against their political enemies in the first night(s) after a potential rise to power. Such a single outburst did not happen, although many people were killed or sent to concentration camps over the following months. When the purge took place in 1934, the expression was transferred to this event (which was of course of rather a different nature).
